text:
maria: Heads-up — BigBank's security team just sent a formal request: they need a tenant-pinned model for EU production, plus a signed artifact bundle and reproducible inference for a set of compliance prompts. Deadline = EOW.
ajay: Is that contractual or a pre-sales ask?
maria: Clause in their SLA amendment. It's gating their go-live.
kim: Understood. We should avoid retraining. Two options: pin an existing build (v2.1) and produce a forensic artifact pack, or create a deterministic adapter that post-processes outputs to match their canonical set. Adapter may be riskier for edge cases.
leo: Timeline-wise pinning an existing build + audit seems fastest. We need to validate determinism across our builds: non-quantized GPU, quantized GPU, and quantized CPU.
sarah: What does their "reproducible inference" requirement look like? exact token match? seed + server config?
maria: They specified: exact-match for 25 compliance prompts, reproducible with identical model binary + config + RNG seed, and an artifacts manifest (model hash, artifact signature, quantization recipe, docker image digest, server cfg). Latency target: p95 <= 220ms on EU region for their traffic mix.
rachel: Quantization is likely the blocker. Some quant kernels are non-deterministic depending on fused ops. We need eng-runtime to pin rollout kernels and log kernel versions.
ajay: Proposal: Create a "forensics-lite" bench: 25 canonical prompts (provided by BigBank), plus 200 anonymized production-like prompts (sampled). Run each variant twice and assert deterministic token traces for canonical set. Capture embeddings, tokenization diffs, latency and resource metrics.
kim: Add acceptance criteria: canonical prompts -> exact token trace match after normalization (lowercasing, unicode normalization, punctuation spacing). For sampling set, allow <= 3 token top-k shifts per prompt and track per-prompt divergence stats.
leo: I can allocate a 3xA10G canary pool for 12h tomorrow. Need automation to run bench and produce artifact bundle.
sarah: I'll assemble the canonical set and a normalization script. Suggest storing artifacts in https://git.redwood/company/forensics (private).
maria: We should offer BigBank two deliverables: (A) pinned model endpoint + model hash header, (B) signed artifact bundle (manifest + deterministic run logs + kernel list).
rachel: For short-term, expose a tenant-scoped route that maps to the pinned binary and returns X-Model-Hash and X-Kernel-Hashes headers. Ops can inject KMS signature into the artifact bundle.
kim: Draft canary manifest snippet (for ops handoff):
```
route: /v1/generate?tenant=bigbank-eu
model: redwood/v2.1-2025-03-01
pinned: true
headers:
  X-Model-Hash: true
  X-Kernel-Hashes: true
canary_pool: canary-3a10
```
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: model=redwood/v2.1-2025-03-01 pool=canary-3a10 window=12h (automated) :gear:
maria: Negotiation points with BigBank: 1) Are they OK with quantized variant if we include kernel hashes and deterministic bench? 2) If EU p95 can't be met with shared fleet, request a commercial SLA credit or deploy a dedicated pool (paid).
ajay: Tech tradeoffs: dedicated pool solves latency but costs more. Quantized variant reduces cost but may affect determinism unless we fix kernels. We should present both options in the comms.
sarah: Also flag downstream impact: tenant-scoped pin might affect traffic shaping and autoscale; ops should reserve capacity and put guardrails.
rachel: I'll prep manifest signing flow and include KMS artifact signature. Legal needs to sign off on artifact contents before we hand to customer. Looping in @legal.
kim: Steps: (1) sarah produce canonical prompts + norm script (today), (2) leo + kim run forensics-lite on v2.1 across variants (tomorrow, 12h), (3) rachel prepare artifact signing + tenant route (tomorrow), (4) maria draft comms & negotiation options (today).
maria: I'll tell BigBank we plan to deliver forensic artifacts and a pinned endpoint by Friday EOD, and include both cost/performance options.
ajay: If we see non-determinism in quantized builds, propose a mitigation timeline: kernel pin + rebuild (3 working days) or dedicated unquantized pool (commercial).
leo: I'll capture perf traces + kernel versions. If we need to rebuild, we should also run regression suites — that adds time.
sarah: Small ask: include a human-readable audit README in the bundle explaining test matrix, commands, and expected hashes.
rachel: Noted. Also will add logging hooks so customer can request replay logs for audit.
maria: Thanks team. Please post updates in this thread. If blockers appear, escalate to eng-leads. :thumbsup:
